newsitem.title: FRANCE: Poll says 96% of French pessimistic about economy.
newsitem.headline: Poll says 96% of French pessimistic about economy.

text.p: Ninety-six percent of French voters feel "anxious" or "morose" about the economic and social situation in France, according to an opinion poll released on Tuesday.

The BVA poll for Paris Match weekly magazine showed that 74 percent of those questioned felt anxiety and 22 percent were morose while only three percent were confident about the current state of affairs in France where unemployment is at a record high of 12.6 percent.
In addition, 67 percent of participants said they do not believe in an economic recovery in 1997, compared to 23 percent who do.

A majority -- 73 percent against 14 percent -- reckon that Prime Minister Alain Juppe is wrong to say there is no alternative to his policy of giving priority to cutting public deficits before reducing unemployment.
Juppe's centre-right government is trying to reduce France's deficit to three percent of gross national product by 1997, the main criteria to qualify for a single European currency.
